newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 6.5/7.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 6.5/7.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 6.5/7.0 percent on Wednesday morning in an ample market.
Dealers said an early central bank injection of 731 billion rupiah helped keep the market ample.
They said money was also returning to the system as people had returned to Jakarta from the long Eid al-Fitr celebration.

But one local bank dealer said operators were made alert after some rises in tom/next and spot/next swaps on worry over possible tightening due to higher weekly tax payments ahead of the end of the fiscal year on March 31.
Overnight swaps edged down to 0.10/0.15 from 0.15/0.25.
But tom/next and spot/next swaps inched up slightly to 0.25/0.35 and 0.90/1.00, respectively. One-month money was at 12.5 percent while three-month was at 13.75 percent.
One Japanese bank dealer attributed the relatively expensive three-month rate to the new reserve requirement rate of five percent effective from April 16.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 8.98 percent, compared with 7.67 percent on Monday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable in quite trading. But one said foreign buyers were seen interested in some medium-term notes.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was last at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
